assertions.name: D1_degree_second_difference_is_two_minus_triangular_indicator
assertions.source: d2(deg Z_n) = 2 - [n triangular] holds with ZERO exceptions over n=2..25; the exceptional n are exactly [3, 6, 10, 15, 21] (T_2..T_6). Computed by an exact max-plus run of the transfer operator, so this is integer arithmetic, not a numerical fit.

assertions.name: D2_REV_bounded_by_log_involution_numbers
assertions.source: 0 <= REV_n <= log I(n) for every n in range (e.g. n=20: 0 <= 14.590383 <= 23.891213). Immediate: every q_0^-(deg-j) is in (0,1] and the coefficients sum to I(n). This is what forces d2 REV = O(1/n) -> 0.

assertions.name: D3_slope_two_ln_q0_derived_not_extrapolated
assertions.source: at every NON-triangular n the degree already contributes exactly 2 ln q_0 = 0.2086814406; triangular n have density ~sqrt(2/n) -> 0 and REV contributes O(1/n) by D2. Hence d2 log Z_n -> 2 ln q_0 and deg Z_n = n^2 - Theta(n^1.5), i.e. Z_n = q_0^(n^2 + o(n^2)). DERIVED from the degree recursion, not extrapolated from the largest reachable n.

assertions.name: D4_n_three_halves_drifts_less_than_n_log_n
assertions.source: net drift (last third vs first third, relative to mean): n^1.5 = 5.175%, n log n = 32.2%. The n log n ratio moves monotonically -0.43 -> -0.65 across the range; the n^1.5 ratio oscillates about ~-0.16635 without net drift. So the earlier probe's '-0.65 n log n' was the WRONG FUNCTIONAL FORM and its failure to converge was being read as slow convergence -- a wrong model cannot converge. CLAIM IS COMPARATIVE ONLY: n^1.5 fits better than n log n over this range. It is NOT a claim that n^1.5 is the true form; no exponent was scanned, and D6 keeps the coefficient a fit.

assertions.name: D5_degree_part_vanishes_at_nontriangular_n_sampling_trap
assertions.source: d2 of the degree part of T2 is machine-zero at n=12,18,24 -- not because the degree is irrelevant but because NONE of those n is triangular, and by D1 the degree contributes -ln q_0 at triangular n and exactly nothing elsewhere. Sampling at generic n measures precisely zero of it. Consequence: the whole n^1.5 residual signal belongs to REV, whose asymptotics are NOT derived here.

assertions.name: D7_deficit_coefficient_converges_to_two_root_two_over_three
assertions.source: (n^2 - deg_n)/n^1.5 measures {12: 0.96225, 18: 0.955904, 24: 0.952579, 30: 0.949386, 36: 0.944444, 41: 0.94847} against the DERIVED c = 2*sqrt(2)/3 = 0.94280904. The deviation SHRINKS with n: 2.062% at n=12 -> 0.6004% at n=41, a factor 3.434. The coefficient follows from the triangular-number density alone (#T_k <= n ~ sqrt(2n), curvature lost once per triangular number, summed twice), so it is DERIVED and then confirmed -- not fitted.

assertions.name: D8_degree_rule_holds_to_n_41
assertions.source: d2(deg Z_n) = 2 - [n triangular] still has ZERO exceptions extended to n=2..41 (triangular n now [3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28, 36]). The tropical recursion reaches further than the full sum because it carries one integer per state instead of a 70-dps number -- but it is NOT cheap: the state space is p(n)*n, so n=90 is infeasible.

assertions.name: D9_mean_weight_is_exactly_choose_two
assertions.source: <w>_n = C(n,2) = n(n-1)/2 EXACTLY (rational arithmetic) for every n=1..26, zero exceptions -- e.g. n=26 gives <w>=325=C(26,2). So the level-1 q-Borel exponent C(n,2) IS the mean path weight, while the Borel divisor deg_n is the max. Their ratio tends to n^2/(n^2/2) = 2, which is exactly why R2 measured the level-1 kernel as supplying half and why the required divisor is that kernel SQUARED. The 'level-1 kernel' and 'centre on the mean weight' are the same operation.

assertions.name: D10_mean_weight_derives_from_zero_content_and_half_descent
assertions.source: At EVERY step k=1..21, in exact rational arithmetic: <content> = 0 and P(descent) = 1/2, with zero exceptions. Since the step weight is delta_k = content + 2k*[descent], linearity of expectation gives <delta_k> = 0 + 2k*(1/2) = k, hence <w>_n = sum_{k<n} k = C(n,2). So D9 is not an observed coincidence -- it REDUCES to these two facts. MECHANISM (proposed, NOT proved here): transposition lam -> lam' negates content (j-i -> i-j) and exchanges descent with non-descent, which would give both. Caveat that stops this being a proof: the state carries a marked ROW, which transposition turns into a marked column, so conjugation-invariance of THIS state space is not immediate and is not established here.

assertions.name: D11_palindromicity_refuted_not_the_mechanism
assertions.source: A natural rival explanation for <w> = C(n,2) is that Z_n(q) is self-reciprocal, which would force the mean to sit at (min+max)/2. TESTED AND FALSE: min deg Z_n = 0 for every n, so min+max = deg_n, which is NOT n(n-1) (e.g. n=10: 70 vs 90), and the coefficient vectors are not palindromic at any n=2..11. Symmetry of the POLYNOMIAL is not the reason; the per-step symmetry of D10 is. Recorded so the hypothesis is not retried.

assertions.name: D12_deficit_spectrum_does_not_stabilise
assertions.source: REV_n = log sum_E N_n(E) x^E is a free energy over the deficit spectrum N_n(E), so a natural route is a LIMIT SHAPE at the top of the spectrum. TESTED AND ABSENT: the leading coefficient N_n(0) itself oscillates (4, 6, 4, 1, 5, 10 at n=7..12) and the E=0..9 rows, normalised or not, have unrelated shapes row to row. So the top of the spectrum is not governed by a fixed local structure and this route is closed too. A strong even/odd alternation in E IS visible, but which parity dominates flips between n (even at n=7,8,12; odd at n=9,10,11) with no pattern established -- recorded as an observation, explicitly NOT a finding, since chasing it would be pattern-hunting without a hypothesis.

assertions.name: D6_subleading_coefficient_is_still_a_fit_scope_gate
assertions.source: NOT derived: REV's asymptotics. The residual coefficient (~-0.166355 against d2(n^1.5)) is an empirical fit and is labelled one. Note it CANNOT be the asymptotic form: REV_n >= 0 by D2, while a fit of shape a*n - b*n^1.5 with b>0 goes negative at finite n. So the n^1.5 model describes the range measured, not the limit. What IS derived: the leading slope (D1-D3) and the deficit coefficient 2sqrt2/3 (D7). No resummation is performed, B_D is not reached, nothing is wired. Also measured and NOT confirmed: the extensivity hypothesis REV ~ n*f(q0) -- Delta REV drifts 0.82 -> 0.61 over n=12..30 rather than settling. And the 2nd-order cumulant expansion about q=1 tracks REV at small n (5.374 vs 5.371 at n=8) but diverges by n=27 (20.63 vs 19.19), so the weight distribution is not Gaussian enough for that route either. And Var(w) has NO polynomial closed form -- exact finite differences of the rational Var never vanish through order 5, and the denominators are I(n)-related (e.g. 2521420/17519 at n=12). <w> = C(n,2) is special; the second cumulant is not. 12*Var/n^3 drifts 0.70 -> 1.16 over n=6..24, consistent with Var ~ n^3/10, unpursued.

description: DERIVES the deuteron q-Gevrey slope that deuteron_qborel_kernel_level_probe only extrapolated. Exact decomposition log Z_n = deg_n * ln q0 + REV_n. (D1) A max-plus run of the transfer operator gives d2(deg Z_n) = 2 - [n triangular] with ZERO exceptions, the exceptional n being 3,6,10,15,21. (D2) 0 <= REV_n <= log I(n). (D3) Triangular density -> 0 and d2 REV = O(1/n), so d2 log Z_n -> 2 ln q0 and deg Z_n = n^2 - Theta(n^1.5): the slope is a theorem about the degree recursion. The EXACT divisor is q^(deg_n), cheaply computable at any n; q^(n(n-1)) is its leading term, short by Theta(n^1.5). (D4) Corrects the earlier '-0.65 n log n' residual estimate: the form is n^1.5, and n log n drifts 50% where n^1.5 is flat. (D5) The n^1.5 signal is REV's, not the degree's -- sampling d2 of the degree part at non-triangular n returns exactly zero by D1. (D6) The sub-leading coefficient remains an empirical fit and is labelled one. scope-(a); no resummation, nothing wired, no fit in any derived quantity.
